utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom and those assisting us outside this courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-10/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ranko Cesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Cesic, first of all, I'd like to be informed whether you can hear me in a language you understand. Could you please put on your mic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cesic. Today we have a Status Conference, and I'd first like to be informed about the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour; good morning, counsel. My name is Mark Harmon. I'm appearing for the Prosecutor. Appearing with me, Mr. Tom Hannis to my immediate right; and to his right, Ms. Susan Grogan, who is the case manager. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. May I have the appearance the for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, all. On behalf of the accused, Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon, Mr. Bakrac. I do understand only recently a meeting took place with the senior legal officer in which you discussed already some items. But before going through the agenda, I'd first like to be informed, Mr. Bakrac, whether you have been fully informed by previous counsel and whether you received all the documents you need in order to defend Mr. Cesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In the second half of January of this year, my esteemed colleague the previous counsel gave me all the supporting material that he received from the Prosecution and, of course, I began to familiarise myself with it at once, so there is no obstacle to our holding the Status Conference today and discussing all the issues which you think should be discussed at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Then I'd perhaps first clarify an issue as to where we stand in view of the position of Mr. Cesic. As you are aware of the -- a new amended indictment has been filed. It was on the 26th of November. In the previous decision by the Chamber, it was indicated that the Chamber considered the plea as entered on the previous indictment would stand and invited the Defence, if there would be any need to enter a different plea, that the Chamber would wait for the initiative of the Defence. I take it, as far as it stands now, that the plea is unchanged also for the new indictment. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. In my humble opinion, I fully agree with the Trial Chamber, and I feel that there is really no need at this point in time to have the accused enter a new plea on all the counts of the indictment, and I think there is no formal necessity for this either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then that's clear. Then I would like to go through some standard items we usually discuss during a Status Conference. The first is - but I think that matter has been settled already - that there are no outstanding disclosure issues. I'd like to hear first from the Prosecution whether the Prosecution deems that it has fulfilled all its disclosure obligations, and then I'll hear from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have disclosed all of the relevant material that we are required to under the Rules to the Defence, and we have done that a considerable time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would agree with that, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no reason whatsoever to doubt what my learned friend Mr. Harmon has said. I only wish to add that from the moment I became counsel in this case, I have not received anything new from the Prosecution. Everything I have received from the previous counsel, and this is what he received from the Prosecution that I have. But I really have no reason to doubt that my learned friend Mr. Harmon has fulfilled all his obligations under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And since he told us he did that already quite some time ago, it's not surprising that you didn't received any new material recently. So there are no outstanding disclosure issues. Since you have been appointed only recently, Mr. Bakrac, perhaps you could inform me whether there has been any further discussions or development of working plans together with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I already have some experience at this Tribunal, and I believe many things can be solved in cooperation with the Prosecution to ensure a fair and expeditious trial and to facilitate matters for the Trial Chamber. So it was my intention to establish contact right after this Status Conference. However, my learned friend Mr. Harmon was quicker than me, and he proposed, together with Mr. Harhoff, a meeting which we have already agreed on. We have yet to agree on the date, but I believe that we will intensify our meetings in order to solve all outstanding issues and to ensure an expeditious trial. I promise that I will always be available for such contacts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Having heard your words, and since I hear no objections from the Prosecution, there's no need to encourage the parties since they are already inclined to solve whatever issues are outstanding. But otherwise, I certainly would have encouraged you. Then may I ask a few questions to the Prosecution. Would the Chamber have to expect on a short term any additional requests or any requests in respect of protective measures, or is that an issue that bothers the Prosecution at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At this moment we have no concerns with respect to protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Could I also ask you whether the Prosecution intends to rely on taking judicial notice of any adjudicated facts? Is there anything to be expected in that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is matter I cannot address at this moment with Your Honour because I need to discuss that with my colleague who is not here, Mr. Tochilovsky.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will inform Mr. Harhoff as soon as I have those discussions with Mr. Tochilovsky and then he can inform you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it's unnecessary, but if the Prosecution would consider to rely on the Jelisic case, of course there might be some problems in relation to the fully adjudicated character of those facts. I'm just asking your attention for that, that if you would consider any further steps in this direction, that the Chamber at least is aware of potential problems in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We are as well. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then my next question would be when the Prosecution would be in a position to file the list of witnesses, exhibits, and 92 bis statements, if any. When do you expect that the Prosecution could file those lists?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We could file those lists with very short notice. However, given the change in counsel situation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- I would like to explore with my colleague from the Defence whether or not this case should go to trial, under what circumstances and the like. But we are prepared for trial. We are ready for trial now. Should the Court wish us to file those matters, such as the witness lists and statements, we could do that. But think it would be prudent at this point to get acquainted with my colleague from the Defence and explore matters that may and could possibly result in this matter not going to trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, I do understand that you would be ready on short notice to file it, but perhaps it would be wiser for the Chamber also not to urge you to do it immediately but first wait and see whether the discussions between the parties would create any new perspectives in this case. But if not, then I think it would be -- it would be good to have those lists, under unchanged circumstances, to have these lists not later than mid-July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. That is our position. We agree with Your Honour, and we will be prepared to file at the Court's direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the reasons why I'm perhaps not urging that much the parties at this very moment is that if I look at this case, which is a not-too-complex case compared to other cases that this Tribunal hears, this case could be ready for trial, I would say, at a relatively short term. But if I look at the cases still to be heard by Trial Chamber I which are cases of considerable length, then even if the case would be ready for trial, that would not mean that without additional measures that the trial could really start. So therefore, let's see whether the discussions between the parties bring anything new. And you will understand that if the perspectives for a trial that would start soon in this Tribunal would not be available, that it's part of the -- it's part of the policy of this Tribunal to see whether certain cases can be transferred back to the state that were part of the former Yugoslavia. So we would have to consider that issue as well. And I would like the parties to be aware of that, that it's still uncertain how we'll proceed, either in this Tribunal or in whatever other way. Of course it's also clear, I think, to the parties that a full trial takes quite some time, and it will keep the Trial Chamber busy full time; whereas under other circumstances, of course, matters might be speeded up. This is a few -- these are a few observations in view of the perspective of this case, and the Chamber is not very happy that when a case is ready for trial, that it would take considerable time to really start trial. But that's a situation that does exist, and I just cannot change that by giving orders. It's -- it's reality, and we have to see how to cope with that reality. These were the issues I was very much interested to hear about. But of course, it's not only my wishes but also what the parties would like to bring to my attention at this very moment that I would like to hear about. Mr. Bakrac, since you're new, you might have more wishes even than the Prosecution, who is already involved in this case for a longer period of time. Is there anything you'd like to bring to my attention at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I believe that we have touched upon all outstanding issues and that the contacts which the Prosecution and the Defence plan to have will help to clarify the situation. In view of what you said just now, Your Honour, the Defence will do its very best, and I undertake to do this, to prepare the case for trial as soon as possible. I have looked at the transcript of the previous Status Conference which was attended by my learned friend when the issue of the possible transfer of this case to one of the former republics, and to that my learned friend replied this trial could be completed quite fast. I agree with this, and I feel that with good cooperation with the Prosecution and the Defence, the case can be prepared quite soon and that this can be done even before the technical pre-conditions are met in the republics of the former Yugoslavia. I feel I have to say this in the interests of my client and his right to an expeditious trial. If we get the case ready for trial and the technical possibilities for a trial in one of the republics of the former Yugoslavia are not yet in place, I believe it's in the interest of my client, in view of his right to an expeditious trial, that the case be completed here before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to give you already a brief response to your observations, Mr. Bakrac, the problem in the Tribunal is not that this case could not be heard in a relatively short period of time, but I just refer to the agenda of Trial Chamber I. If you would look at it, you would see that two major cases, both taking at least one year but presumably two years each case, are on the agenda to start soon. Since Trial Chamber I consists of two sections, three Judges in each section, they're busy for the next one or two years. So a solution has to be found in whatever way, either transferring the case to other Trial Chambers. But if I look at the agendas of other Trial Chambers, you might see a similar picture. And it's because of this, if you could call it congestion, that of course we have to take into consideration all options, especially since your client is entitled as well to an expeditious trial. So therefore, I mentioned it in order to -- not to hide this major problem from you so that you can take that into consideration as well, that the perspectives in this Trial Chamber are not very optimistic, not very positive, and that the Tribunal has to explore whatever is possible to see that this relatively small case - I'm not saying is unimportant case but not as complex and extensive as other cases - will be dealt with also as soon as possible. I just gave you a small impression about our agenda and of the agenda of the Tribunal as a whole, but I am aware -- of course, I would fully agree that we should not wait to hear cases just for the reason that perhaps in the future there might be a possibility to transfer a case back to one of the republics of the former Yugoslavia, and I think no one would ever have that in his mind. On the other hand, we have the practical problems I just explained to you. Is there anything else you would like to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am deeply grateful for your exhaustive explanation. I have nothing else to raise at present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Harmon, is there anything the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is nothing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Cesic, both counsel for the Prosecution and for your defence have raised the issues they thought of importance, but let's not forget it's not their case but it's your case. Is there anything you would like to bring to my attention at this very moment, including whatever concerns you might have about your present conditions in the Detention Unit or your personal situation including health. Is there anything you would like to bring to my attention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At present, my health is good, and the conditions in the Detention Unit are also good. I have a new Defence counsel, and we have been in contact frequently, and we are working on the case. I leave all formal and legal matters to Mr. Bakrac for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that you rely on counsel and that there are no specific personal matters you would like to raise at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Cesic. Since there seems to be nothing on the agenda any more, the Chamber would like to invite the parties to inform the Chamber as to the development of their discussions; not the development, but if it results in anything the Chamber would have to know. You don't have to keep us updated on your discussions, especially not on where you agree and disagree. The Chamber would also like to be informed at the earliest possible stage if there would be any agreement on the facts, because that, I take it, will also be part of your discussions apart from other issues. Being there nothing on the agenda any more, we will adjourn.
